fact.box: Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (formerly the GST/HST credit), paid by the CRA
fact.claim: For July 2026 to June 2027, a single person with no children can get up to $679 from the CRA. The amount is based on the 2025 tax return. The GST/HST credit was renamed the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit in July 2026. The $679 is a $445 base amount plus a $234 single supplement, and the supplement only phases in once income is above $11,564, so a single person with very low income gets less than the full $679. The benefit shrinks once family net income passes $46,432.

caption:
🐶⛏️ If you skip filing, up to $679 in grocery money never reaches you.

The CRA works out this grocery money from your 2025 tax return, so no return means nothing to pay you from. Plenty skip it because they owe no tax, and that's how the money slips away.

plain.what: The GST/HST credit is money the CRA sends people to help with groceries. The CRA is the government office that handles taxes. In July 2026 this money got a new name, the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit, and for July 2026 to June 2027 a single person with no kids can get up to $679.
plain.so_what: The CRA works out that $679 from your 2025 tax return, so if you never file, there is nothing for them to pay you from, even when you owe no tax.
plain.do: Check today whether your 2025 tax return was filed, and write the answer down.
